problem.text: A sequence of numbers is defined recursively by $a_1 = 1$, $a_2 = \frac{3}{7}$, and $$a_n = \frac{a_{n-2}\cdot a_{n-1}}{2a_{n-2} - a_{n-1}}$$ for all $n \geq 3$ Then $a_{2019}$ can be written as $\frac{p}{q}$, where $p$ and $q$ are relatively prime positive integers. What is $p+q$?

steps.title: Where to start: compute a few terms
steps.body: Term number $2019$ is much too far to reach one step at a time, so the answer must come from a pattern. The quickest way to find one is to compute the next couple of terms and compare them with $a_1$ and $a_2$.

steps.title: Spot the pattern
steps.body: Next, $a_4 = \frac{\frac{3}{7}\cdot \frac{3}{11}}{\frac{6}{7} - \frac{3}{11}} = \frac{9/77}{45/77} = \frac{1}{5} = \frac{3}{15}$. If we also write $a_1 = \frac{3}{3}$, the first four terms are $\frac{3}{3}, \frac{3}{7}, \frac{3}{11}, \frac{3}{15}$: the numerator stays $3$ and the denominator goes up by $4$ each time.

your_turn.prompt: Write a formula for the denominator of $a_n$ in terms of $n$ that fits $n = 1, 2, 3, 4$.

steps.title: Why the pattern keeps going: flip to reciprocals
steps.body:
A guess from four terms is not a proof, so take reciprocals of the rule and split the fraction:
$$\frac{1}{a_n} = \frac{2a_{n-2} - a_{n-1}}{a_{n-2}a_{n-1}} = \frac{2}{a_{n-1}} - \frac{1}{a_{n-2}}.$$ This says $\frac{1}{a_n} - \frac{1}{a_{n-1}} = \frac{1}{a_{n-1}} - \frac{1}{a_{n-2}}$, so the reciprocals go up by the same amount every time: they form an arithmetic sequence.

your_turn.prompt: What is the common difference $\frac{1}{a_2} - \frac{1}{a_1}$, and what formula for $\frac{1}{a_n}$ follows?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: So $a_{2019} = \frac{3}{4\cdot 2019 - 1} = \frac{3}{8075}$. This is in lowest terms, because the digits of $8075$ add to $20$, so $3$ does not divide $8075$. Then $p + q = 3 + 8075 = 8078$. The answer is **(E)**.
